svg.title: Capture and index update lifecycle
svg.desc: The watcher captures changed client families, retains previous documents for unchanged or failed families, applies exclusions and writes the corpus and manifest. Capture alone ends there. The watcher chooses recent or archive builds, stages corpus copies and rebuilds with local Contriever and LEANN. It validates the candidate, publishes it with rollback for a failed swap, validates the published index, records tier state, and restarts the resident search server. Failures are recorded and retried, with a backoff for builds.
svg.text: Capture and index update lifecycle
The watcher runs a cycle about once a minute and can wake earlier when a build finishes.
1. Capture
Check client families
Fingerprint sources and exclusions.
Reparse changed or failed families.
Keep available documents
Keep prior documents for unchanged
or failed families, then apply exclusions.
Write corpus and manifest
Update normalized transcripts, remove
stale files, and save manifest if needed.
capture command ends here
The run watcher continues to the
index decision below.
A failed family is retried on a later capture; documents already rendered during a failed parse can also be kept.
2. Decide which tier needs a build
Recent: session-memory-recent
Documents changed since the archive, plus the canary.
A changed set normally waits 90 seconds of quiet,
with a five-minute maximum wait. A missing index is due.
Requires an archive and normally at most 4,000,000 recent bytes.
Archive: session-memory
All current corpus documents. Build if missing or empty,
when recent documents exceed 4,000,000 bytes, or to purge
exclusions after 90 seconds of quiet. Force can request either tier.
A tier already building cannot start another build.
Failed builds normally wait 15 minutes before retry. Force bypasses the backoff; one-shot runs bypass the recent debounce.
3. Build and publish each due tier
Stage and rebuild
Copy corpus files for the build.
Local Contriever and LEANN
rebuild the staged index.
Validate candidate
Search for the canary.
A failed check stops publication.
Publish
Move the candidate into place.
A failed swap attempts to restore
the previous index.
Validate published index
Search for the canary again.
Only a successful check returns
tier state for the watcher to save.
A published validation failure is recorded for retry; the previous index is not restored at that point.
4. Collect the result and continue
Save state and restart search server
After a successful build, the watcher saves tier state and restarts
the resident server in a continuous run so it loads the new index.
Wait for the next cycle or a build result
Errors are recorded. Capture and eligible builds are retried in later cycles;
the watcher also restarts a stopped server during continuous runs.
